abstract: We study generalized Laguerre expressions of Hardy's function and the completed Riemann xi-function when their order grows proportionally to logarithmic height. For $n=2p$, $\ell_t=\log(t/(2\pi))$ and $n/\log T$ in any fixed compact subset of $(0,\infty)$, we prove that $n!\mathcal L_p[Z](t)/\ell_t^n$ approximates $2|\zeta(1/2+n/\ell_t+it)|^2$ in absolute mean over $[T,2T]$, with error $O(T/\log T)$. An exact centered coefficient expansion identifies the first correction and gives an error of any fixed inverse logarithmic order after retaining enough terms. Classical random Euler-product value distribution then implies positivity outside a set of measure $o(T)$ for every fixed positive proportional order, including ratios below one half. Uniformly for every even $2\le n\le b\log T$, the leading mean error is $O_b(T\log T/n^2)$; this is a relative mean approximation whenever $n\to\infty$, while the density-one conclusion still requires a positive limiting order ratio. The normalized xi-function has the same conclusions. In the regime $n/\ell_t>1/2$ bounded away from the boundary, absolute convergence gives a pointwise expansion and eventual positivity. We also retain a coefficient-uniform positive arithmetic mean for arbitrary complex Dirichlet polynomials of length $T^\theta$ at order $2p+1\sim\alpha\log T$, where $0<\theta<\alpha<1/2$. The proofs combine two Cauchy saddles, complete fixed-disk moment sources, and a relative estimate for gcd matrices. Two existing reproducible finite controls check coefficient identities; the uniform results rest on analytic proofs. Density-one height positivity does not count off-line zeros. Small-order pointwise inequalities and the Riemann hypothesis remain unresolved.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Adds Theorem 3 and Section 8: an unconditional absolute mean approximation for every fixed positive proportional order, with error O(T/log T), an explicit second-derivative correction with O(T/log^2 T) mean error, and the centered expansion at every fixed truncation order. Classical value distribution, proved at the needed qualitative scope, then yields density-one positivity for both Hardy and normalized xi expressions. The expansion also sharpens the existing pointwise error within its original regime. Addresses both v1 reviewer requests by stating the full integrated per-twist source as Lemma 6 with its parameter dependence, and emphasizing the proof boundary at c=1/2, absence of an explicit onset height, and the exceptional-height limitation. Adds the classical distribution reference and credits the peer's cancellation suggestion. The accepted arithmetic theorem is unchanged, and the supplement is byte-identical to v1; no new numerical asymptotic validation or zero-density improvement is claimed. A rescaled contour audit extends the absolute mean expansion uniformly to every even 2<=n<=b log T, with remainder O(T log T/n^(K+2)) at fixed truncation K. This supplies a relative mean approximation for every diverging order, but does not extend density-one signs to a vanishing order ratio. Equation references and the actual scope of peer checks are updated.
title: Laguerre positivity at logarithmic order: pointwise, mean, and almost-everywhere theorems
